import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source5_44_4 with Source5_44_1 on Cust_id
df = source4.merge(source1, on="Cust_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_44_0 on Ord_id
df = df.merge(source0, on="Ord_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_44_2 on Prod_id
df = df.merge(source2, on="Prod_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source5_44_3 on Ship_id
df = df.merge(source3, on="Ship_id", how="inner")

# Group by Customer_Segment (primary key) to ensure uniqueness and match target keys
df = df.groupby("Customer_Segment", as_index=False).first()

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df = df[["Customer_Segment", "Ord_id", "Prod_id", "Ship_id", "Cust_id"]]

# Convert Ord_id, Prod_id, Ship_id, Cust_id to integer by extracting numeric part
# The target schema expects these as integers, source has strings like 'Ord_1', 'Prod_1', etc.

def extract_int(col):
    return col.str.extract(r'(\d+)').astype(int)

df["Ord_id"] = extract_int(df["Ord_id"])
df["Prod_id"] = extract_int(df["Prod_id"])
df["Ship_id"] = extract_int(df["Ship_id"])
df["Cust_id"] = extract_int(df["Cust_id"])

# Write output to target file
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_44/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
